samples.q1: How often should the AC be cleaned?
samples.a1: Every 4–6 months for a unit that runs daily.
samples.q2: Do you also clean fan coil units in older Dubai buildings where the unit sits above a false ceiling and access is only through a small hatch?
samples.a2: Yes. The technician checks the hatch size first; if the unit cannot be reached safely, we send photos and agree on the next step before any work starts, so you never pay for a visit that cannot be completed.

samples.longParagraph: Our technicians arrive with drop sheets, a wet-vacuum and their own ladder, so there is nothing to prepare except clear access to the indoor unit. After the clean you get before-and-after photos in WhatsApp and a note on anything that needs attention later. If a part has to be replaced, we send the price first and wait for your approval.
samples.longButton: Book a deep clean for all five split units in the villa this Saturday
samples.diagSummary: Most likely the indoor coil and the drain line are dirty: the musty smell and the dripping point the same way. A standard clean usually fixes both; the technician confirms on site.
samples.diagCause1Title: Dust and mould on the coil
samples.diagCause1Text: Dubai humidity turns coil dust into a film that smells when the fan starts.
samples.diagCause2Text: Condensate backs up in the tray and drips from the unit.
samples.diagQuestion1: How old is the unit and when was it last cleaned?
samples.diagQuestion2: Does the water appear only while cooling, or also when the unit is off?
samples.diagSafety: If water is reaching a socket or the ceiling light, switch the unit off at the breaker until the visit.

Diagnose.privacy: The photo is analysed, not stored. No name or phone needed.

smell.summary: A musty smell when the unit starts almost always comes from a film of dust and mould on the indoor coil and in the drain tray. A standard clean removes it; the technician confirms on site.
smell.cause1: Dust and mould on the coil
smell.cause1Text: Dubai humidity turns coil dust into a film that smells when the fan starts.
smell.cause2: Standing water in the drain tray
smell.cause2Text: A slow drain keeps condensate in the tray, where bacteria grow.
smell.question: When was the unit last cleaned?

drip.summary: Water from the indoor unit usually means the drain line is silted or the coil has iced up behind a dirty filter. A standard clean clears the drain; the technician checks the filter and the slope of the pipe.
drip.cause1Text: Condensate backs up in the tray and overflows.
drip.cause2Text: A clogged filter starves the airflow, the coil freezes and drips as it melts.
drip.question: Does it drip only while cooling, or after the unit is off too?

weak.summary: Weak cooling with the unit running all day points to a coil and blower caked in dust; after years without service a deep clean restores the airflow. If it stays weak, the technician checks the refrigerant.
weak.cause1: Coil and blower caked in dust
weak.cause1Text: Airflow drops and the unit never reaches the set temperature.
weak.cause2Text: A slow leak lowers cooling over months; checked with gauges on site.
weak.question: How old is the unit, and when was it last serviced?

stain.summary: A fresh coffee stain on light fabric usually lifts with hot-water extraction and a tannin treatment. The technician tests a hidden spot first.
stain.cause1Text: Coffee tannins bind to cotton and linen quickly; the sooner, the easier.
stain.cause2Text: Rubbing or hot water can fix the stain; blotting only is best until the visit.
stain.question: What is the sofa fabric, and how old is the stain?
